description: Journey — last, and never for a local engine project (gripforge game-attach works in it). Run gripforge_game_audit then gripforge_validate_release first: export a game whose verdict is complete and whose release is ready, or tell the user what is left. Not for a local engine project: when the game's Godot project already exists on the user's machine, do not export it — attach GripForge to it with the CLI, gripforge game-attach <project_id> <project folder> (addon gripforge_kits + game under gripforge/, never its project.godot, scenes or scripts); Unity / Unreal: gripforge_gamekit_deliver in place. A native project's answer carries notices [{ code: export_not_needed, howToFix }]: follow it. If game-attach reports manual_setup_found, follow its howToFix before any --force. Prepare a download manifest for an existing Game Kit project in the current workspace. Reuses the same player and HUD as hosted play, compiles only installed enabled kit runtimes, and lists the game configuration, static resources and Library assets to download. Does not publish the project or change its visibility. The hosted MCP cannot write local files: use gripforge game-export <project_id> <folder> locally, then npm run dev. The CLI verifies downloads and preserves local edits on updates (--check previews conflicts; --force backs up and replaces edits only when authorized). The delivered versions remain fixed until an explicit export update. Legacy kits and unpublished source overlays cannot be exported. net.* kits still need their online services. 0 credits.
